summary: The First Folio is the first collected edition of William Shakespeare's plays, printed in London in 1623, about seven years after his death. It holds 36 plays, arranged as comedies, histories and tragedies, and 18 of them had never been printed before, including The Tempest, Macbeth and Julius Caesar. Two of Shakespeare's colleagues, John Heminges and Henry Condell, gathered the texts. The scan here is the Boston Public Library copy, shelfmark G.174.1, digitised by the Internet Archive.
context: Heminges and Condell, who prepared the book, said it replaced earlier printings they called stolen and surreptitious. The syndicate was Edward Blount and William and Isaac Jaggard, with William Aspley and John Smethwick as rights holders. Printing probably ran from February 1622 to November 1623. About 750 copies were printed and 235 are known to survive. The Boston copy was bought by Thomas Pennant Barton from Thomas Rodd of London in 1845, and the Library's description notes leaves reattached or supplied from other copies.

people.name: William Shakespeare
people.note: He died at Stratford-upon-Avon on 23 April 1616, seven years before the Folio appeared.

people.name: John Heminges
people.note: Compiled the Folio's contents with Henry Condell; both were colleagues of Shakespeare in the King's Men.

people.name: Henry Condell
people.note: Joint compiler of the Folio with John Heminges.

people.name: Ben Jonson
people.note: Wrote the poem 'To the Reader' that faces the portrait, and is among the contributors of commendatory verses.

people.name: Martin Droeshout
people.note: The engraver of the portrait on the title page.

people.name: Isaac Jaggard
people.note: Printed the book with Edward Blount; he did most of the work after his father William Jaggard, old and blind, died a month before it went on sale.

people.name: Edward Blount
people.note: Bookseller and publisher who shared the venture with the Jaggards.

people.name: Thomas Pennant Barton
people.note: Bought this copy from Thomas Rodd of London in 1845; the Library's Barton collection is named for him.

places.name: London
places.note: Where the Folio was printed and published in 1623.

places.name: Stratford-upon-Avon
places.note: Where Shakespeare died in 1616 and was buried in Holy Trinity Church.

places.name: Oxford, Bodleian Library
places.note: Received its copy in early 1624 and sold it later as a superseded edition.

places.name: Boston Public Library
places.note: Holds this copy in its Rare Books department.

timeline.label: Printing of the Folio probably begins in February.
The Folio is entered in the Stationers' Register on 8 November and published.
Thomas Pennant Barton buys this copy from Thomas Rodd of London.
Barton privately prints a description of his copy as it stood about then or earlier.

ideas.title: Plays saved from loss
ideas.note: Eighteen of the 36 plays, including The Tempest and Macbeth, are not known to have been printed before the Folio.

ideas.title: Folio as a prestige format
ideas.note: Plays usually came out as cheap quartos, while folio was reserved for books of lasting value, so printing plays this way made a claim for them.

ideas.title: Replacing the earlier printings
ideas.note: The editors presented the Folio as the true text that supersedes stolen and maimed copies.

ideas.title: No two copies alike
ideas.note: Corrections were made while printing was under way, so surviving copies differ, and this one has leaves supplied from other copies.
